summary:
The article surveys China’s political changes, major events, disasters, and notable deaths in 2018. The National People’s Congress removed presidential term limits in March, allowing Xi Jinping to remain in office beyond the previous limit. Wang Qishan became vice president, and other senior officials took new posts. Xi also met North Korean leader Kim Jong-un in Beijing.

Severe winter storms killed 10 people and affected more than 567,000. Tropical Storm Rumbia caused 53 deaths in August, while Typhoon Mangkhut disrupted transport in Guangdong in September. Other major stories included criticism of a Spring Festival Gala sketch over blackface, the blocking of Peppa Pig videos, and large tax penalties imposed on actress Fan Bingbing. China marked 40 years of reform and opening-up with a major exhibition in November.

The article also records the deaths of numerous figures in politics, science, and the arts, including novelist Jin Yong.
